# JSON audit → SIEM

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Integrations · **Label:** `feature:audit-log-export` · **Epic:** [#65](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/65) · **Tickets:** 6 (5S 1M)

Each worker can write a separate JSON decision stream, one line per stored analytics event, to stdout, stderr or a rotating file, with verified user identity fields. A SIEM shipper (Vector, Fluent Bit, Splunk UF) can read it without parsing operational logs. The schema is versioned, closed and documented, and never holds bodies, headers, query values or secret values. Two existing gaps are fixed first: swapped secrets can reach Event.URL today, and most deny events have no reason.

## How we build it

- Fix first (W-P1-JAUD-05): swapSecrets in internal/proxy/http.go rewrites s.req.URL.RawQuery with the real secret, and recordAllowEvent, relayMCPSSE and the post-forward event sites then build fullURL from s.req.URL.RequestURI(). The real value can reach SQLite, signed receipts, logDecision lines and central sync. requestScope gains a new auditURL field captured in readRequest before swapSecrets and applyTransforms; every StoreEvent and logDecision site in internal/proxy uses it.
- Deny reasons (W-P1-JAUD-06): every deny site sets Event.Reason from one bounded set shared with Metrics.RecordBlocked (policy, no_tls, judge, dlp, mcp_*; later tickets add headers_too_large (W-P1-VRFY-02), user_blocked (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and identity_required / group_not_allowed (W-P1-GPOL-03) to the same set; attribute-mode identity itself never denies). storeDeny in serve.go stops dropping its reason argument, and a test fails on any deny event with an empty Reason.
- New package internal/auditlog. Record is a closed struct and FromEvent(analytics.Event, Meta) Record is the only mapping from Event. It never marshals Event, so SecretRef, Evidence, bodies, headers and future Event fields cannot leak. Each line is json.Marshal(Record) plus a newline, written in one Write; slog is not used, so no time/level/msg keys appear. p5-otlp should map this Record to OTel attributes instead of keeping a second allowlist.
- Placement off the request path: analytics.WithOnBatch becomes additive (several tees; alerts.Observe uses it today). The auditlog Sink is a tee on the async writer's goroutine, so it sees each event once, after compliance tagging and signing, and is not affected by the managed apply loop rebuilding the TaggingStore. The tee hands each batch to the sink's own bounded channel without blocking; a separate goroutine writes through a bufio.Writer flushed once per batch. A full channel drops the batch and counts it, so a slow disk can never back-pressure the async writer or requests.
- Failure mode: the stream is best effort; the SQLite store and signed receipts stay the record of truth. A write error or drop never blocks or fails a request; it increments a counter and logs a rate-limited WARN without record content. With enabled and output file, a path that cannot be opened fails startup, like signedReceipts.log. The stream does not need the CP or the IdP.
- Config in the existing node-local audit block (Config.Audit is json:"-", restart only): audit.jsonLog {enabled: false, output: stdout|stderr|file, path, maxSizeMB: 100, maxBackups: 10, maxAgeDays: 30, compress: false, fileMode: 0600, query: drop|keys}. Parsed in parseAudit and checked in validateAudit (internal/config/audit.go). Rotation uses gopkg.in/natefinch/lumberjack.v2 pinned in go.mod; the first file is created with fileMode so lumberjack keeps that mode on rotation. When output is stdout, the operational logger moves to stderr so the streams never mix.
- Schema warden.decision.v1, one line per stored event: schema, schema_rev, ts (UTC RFC 3339 nanoseconds), proxy_id (expanded central.proxyId, else os.Hostname()), proxy_id_source, agent_id, boot_id (random per process), seq (per boot, assigned at the tee so drops show as gaps), decision, reason, protocol, domain, port, method, url_path (pre-swap path only, userinfo and fragment removed, max 2 KiB), query_keys (sorted names only, when query: keys), status, latency_ms, tool, provider, cost_usd, dlp_action, dlp_rule, dlp_partial, data_classes, swapped_refs (placeholder names), compliance, judge_reason (max 512 bytes, control characters removed), user{status, sub, email, groups, groups_truncated, sid}, truncated. User fields other than status appear only when status is valid; groups are capped at 64. A whole line is capped at 16 KiB. event_uid is not in v1 because it is only set at central sync.
- Versioning: docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json and warden.admin.v1.json (JSON Schema 2020-12, additionalProperties false). v1 accepts only additive optional fields with a schema_rev bump; Record, schema file and docs change in the same PR, enforced by a reflection test. Consumers must ignore unknown fields. Breaking changes ship as v2 next to v1 for one minor release.
- CP admin lines: the CP reads the same audit.jsonLog block and passes the writer to the p1-admin-audit middleware, which emits warden.admin.v1 lines after the admin audit row is stored. Collectors route both streams on the top-level schema field.
- Metrics in internal/observability, nil-safe: warden.auditlog.lines.total{schema}, warden.auditlog.write_errors.total{reason}, warden.auditlog.dropped.total. A startup INFO line shows output, path and schema version.

## Done when

With audit.jsonLog.enabled: true and output: file on a real worker, every stored analytics event (CONNECT/tcp, HTTPS, MCP over HTTP, SSE and WS, gRPC) produces exactly one line that matches warden.decision.v1, with proxy_id, boot_id and a gap-free seq under normal disk conditions. Every deny line has a non-empty reason from the documented set. User sub, email and groups appear only for valid tokens. A request with a secret placeholder in its query never shows the real value in the line, the SQLite row, the receipt or the operational log. A failing disk increments write or drop counters without failing requests. Files rotate at maxSizeMB and keep at most maxBackups. A CP policy save emits one warden.admin.v1 line, and the documented Vector config ships both streams from the compose recipe into a test sink.

### 1/6 · W-P1-JAUD-05

**Record the pre-swap URL on events and decision logs**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

swapSecrets in internal/proxy/http.go writes the real secret into s.req.URL.RawQuery, and several event sites later build fullURL from s.req.URL.RequestURI(). A placeholder in a query string therefore puts the real value into Event.URL, which goes to SQLite, signed receipts, logDecision and central sync. Capture the URL in readRequest, before swapSecrets and applyTransforms, and use that copy at every StoreEvent and logDecision site. This must land before any export of Event.URL.

**Requirements**

- requestScope gets a new auditURL string field set in readRequest from scheme, s.domain and the original escaped path and query, before swapSecrets and applyTransforms run.
- Every StoreEvent and logDecision call in internal/proxy (http.go, ws.go, grpc.go) that builds a URL uses auditURL instead of s.req.URL.RequestURI().
- The forwarded upstream request is unchanged: the real secret is still swapped into the outgoing query.
- No real secret value appears in Event.URL, the signed receipt, the operational decision log or central sync payloads.
- No config flag: this is a leak fix with no new behaviour; events now carry the placeholder the agent sent.
- No new logging of secret values, headers or bodies is added.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy/http.go: add auditURL to requestScope and set it in readRequest (around the existing fullURL build at line ~327).
2. internal/proxy/http.go: replace the post-swap fullURL builds in recordAllowEvent, relayMCPSSE and the post-forward event sites (~866, ~908, ~1064, ~1104) with s.auditURL.
3. internal/proxy/ws.go and internal/proxy/grpc.go: use the scope's auditURL where they record a URL after the swap.
4. New test in internal/proxy/http_test.go (or a new swap_url_test.go): send a request with ?key=<placeholder> through a proxy with a fake secret source, a signing store and a buffered logger.
5. Assert the upstream test server received the real value, and that the stored Event.URL, the receipt line and the log buffer contain the placeholder and never the real value.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A request to https://api.example.test/v1/x?key=<placeholder> reaches the upstream with the real value in the query.
- [ ] The stored Event.URL contains the placeholder, and the real value is absent from the Event, the signed receipt line and the operational log output.
- [ ] The same holds for an MCP SSE request and an allowed request recorded by recordAllowEvent.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestSwappedQueryNotRecorded` passes, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-JAUD-01`](audit-log-export.md#36--w-p1-jaud-01) Add internal/auditlog decision stream on the async writer tee

### 2/6 · W-P1-JAUD-06

**Set a bounded Reason on every deny event**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Most deny events have an empty Event.Reason today: storeDeny in internal/proxy/serve.go takes a reason and drops it, and the CONNECT deny paths (policy, no_tls) never set it. A SIEM cannot tell a policy deny from a no_tls, judge or DLP deny without it. Fill Reason on every deny site from the same bounded set used by Metrics.RecordBlocked, and document the set.

**Requirements**

- storeDeny sets Event.Reason from its reason argument.
- The CONNECT deny paths in serve.go (policy, no_tls) and every deny StoreEvent in http.go, ws.go, grpc.go and tls.go set Reason.
- Reason values come from one bounded set defined as constants in a new internal/proxy/reasons.go and shared with RecordBlocked calls; free text is never stored in Reason. Later deny reasons (headers_too_large from W-P1-VRFY-02, user_blocked from W-P1-BLOCK-02, identity_required and group_not_allowed from W-P1-GPOL-03) are added to this file by those tickets.
- Existing MCP reasons keep their current values so stored events and dashboards stay compatible.
- Allow events keep an empty Reason.
- No config flag: the field already exists and the change only fills it.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/proxy/reasons.go: constants for policy, no_tls, judge, dlp and the existing mcp_* values, plus a Reasons() list for docs and tests.
2. internal/proxy/serve.go: storeDeny passes reason into the Event; the policy and no_tls paths at ~108 and ~132 set Reason.
3. internal/proxy/http.go, ws.go, grpc.go, tls.go: set Reason on each deny event using the constants that match the existing RecordBlocked call.
4. New test internal/proxy/reasons_test.go: drive each deny path with a recording store and assert Reason is non-empty and in Reasons().
5. docs/architecture.md: list the reason values in the analytics event section.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A CONNECT to a domain not in policy stores a deny event with Reason policy.
- [ ] A CONNECT to a TLS-required domain without TLS stores Reason no_tls; judge and DLP denies store judge and dlp.
- [ ] Every deny event produced in the test run has a Reason contained in Reasons().
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestDenyReasons` passes.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#27--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT, per request and per h2 stream; [`W-P1-GPOL-03`](identity-policy.md#39--w-p1-gpol-03) Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time; [`W-P1-JAUD-02`](audit-log-export.md#46--w-p1-jaud-02) Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests

### 3/6 · W-P1-JAUD-01

**Add internal/auditlog decision stream on the async writer tee**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#66](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/66)

Create new package internal/auditlog that writes one warden.decision.v1 JSON line per stored analytics event to stdout, stderr or a rotating file. The sink runs as a tee on the async analytics writer's goroutine and hands batches to its own bounded queue, so it adds no I/O to the request goroutine and cannot stall the async writer. Config sits under the existing audit block as audit.jsonLog, off by default. Write errors and drops are counted and never fail a request.

**Requirements**

- Config: audit.jsonLog {enabled: false, output: stdout|stderr|file, path, maxSizeMB: 100, maxBackups: 10, maxAgeDays: 30, compress: false, fileMode: 0600, query: drop|keys (default drop)} in internal/config/audit.go. Validation rejects file output without a path, unknown output or query values, and maxSizeMB <= 0. Restart only.
- Record: closed Record struct built only by FromEvent(analytics.Event, Meta); never marshals Event. Fields as listed in the feature design; event_uid is not included.
- Content limits: url_path keeps only the path (no userinfo, fragment or query values), max 2 KiB; query_keys only when query is keys; judge_reason max 512 bytes with control characters removed; groups max 64 with groups_truncated; whole line max 16 KiB with truncated true.
- Identity: user.status is always set when the event has an IdentityStatus; sub, email, groups and sid are written only when status is valid.
- Placement: analytics.WithOnBatch becomes additive so alerts.Observe and the sink both run. The tee assigns seq and enqueues without blocking; a full queue drops the batch and increments warden.auditlog.dropped.total. A single goroutine writes each line with one Write through a bufio.Writer flushed per batch.
- Output: file output uses lumberjack.v2 pinned in go.mod; the first file is created with fileMode. A file that cannot be opened at startup fails startup. When output is stdout, the worker's operational logger is moved to stderr and this is logged once.
- Metrics: nil-safe RecordAuditLogLine(schema), RecordAuditLogWriteError(reason) and RecordAuditLogDropped(n) on observability.Metrics, backed by warden.auditlog.lines.total, warden.auditlog.write_errors.total and warden.auditlog.dropped.total. Error logs are rate limited and never include record content.
- Back-compat: with the block absent or enabled false there is no tee, no goroutine and no change to analytics rows, receipts or fleet ingest.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/audit.go: add JSONLogConfig to AuditConfig, a jsonLog block in rawAudit, defaults in parseAudit and checks in validateAudit; tests in internal/config/audit_test.go.
2. internal/analytics/async.go: change WithOnBatch to append to a slice of tee funcs and call each in order; extend TestAsyncWriter_OnBatchTee for two tees.
3. New internal/auditlog/record.go: Record, Meta{ProxyID, ProxyIDSource, AgentID, BootID} and FromEvent with the URL, query, truncation and identity rules.
4. New internal/auditlog/sink.go: New(cfg config.JSONLogConfig, meta Meta, m *observability.Metrics) (*Sink, error), Observe([]analytics.Event) for the tee, a bounded queue, the writer goroutine, and Close(ctx) that drains the queue and closes lumberjack.
5. internal/observability/observability.go: register the three auditlog counters in newMetrics and add the nil-safe Record methods.
6. internal/worker/worker.go: when pol.Audit.JSONLog.Enabled, build Meta (proxy_id from expandEnv(pol.Central.ProxyID) else os.Hostname(); agent_id from buildJudge), create the Sink, add analytics.WithOnBatch(sink.Observe) to asyncOpts, route the operational logger to stderr for stdout output, and close the sink after asyncStore.Close().
7. Tests: internal/auditlog/record_test.go (URL rules, caps, identity gating), sink_test.go (one line per event, seq order, rotation, file mode after rotation, full queue drops without blocking, failing writer), and internal/worker/analytics_chain_test.go (compliance tags reach the line, a compliance toggle keeps the sink).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With output file, driving an allowed HTTPS request, a policy deny, a no_tls CONNECT deny and a WebSocket upgrade produces as many lines as analytics rows, each with schema warden.decision.v1 and consecutive seq values: `go test -race ./internal/auditlog ./internal/worker -run 'TestDecisionStream|TestAnalyticsChain'`.
- [ ] An Event with URL https://u:p@api.example.test/v1/x?token=abc#frag gives url_path /v1/x and none of token=abc, u:p or #frag; with query keys the line has query_keys ["token"] and still no value.
- [ ] An event with IdentityStatus invalid and a sub claim produces user.status invalid and no user.sub, user.email or user.groups.
- [ ] With maxSizeMB 1 and maxBackups 2, writing 3.5 MB leaves at most one active file plus two backups, all with mode 0600, and no line split across files: `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestRotation`.
- [ ] With a writer that always errors or blocks, 10 tee'd events still produce 10 SQLite rows, the request handler returns its normal status, and write_errors or dropped increases.
- [ ] With output stdout, stdout carries only lines whose schema is warden.decision.v1 and operational records go to stderr.
- [ ] Config `audit: {jsonLog: {enabled: true, output: file}}` with no path, or output syslog, fails to load with an error naming audit.jsonLog: `go test ./internal/config -run TestAuditJSONLogConfig`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#37--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync; [`W-P1-JAUD-05`](audit-log-export.md#16--w-p1-jaud-05) Record the pre-swap URL on events and decision logs

### 4/6 · W-P1-JAUD-02

**Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#67](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/67)

Add docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json and pin it to auditlog.Record with tests, so the schema and the code cannot drift and no unreviewed Event field can reach the stream. The tests compare struct tags with the schema in both directions, check that every analytics.Event field is either mapped or explicitly excluded, and prove that secrets, evidence and header names never appear in a line. No new Go dependency is added.

**Requirements**

- docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json uses JSON Schema 2020-12 with additionalProperties false at every object level, schema as a required const, ts required with format date-time, and reason as an enum taken from the W-P1-JAUD-06 set.
- The schema description states the versioning rule: additive optional fields only in v1 with a schema_rev bump; breaking changes ship as v2 next to v1 for one minor release; consumers ignore unknown fields.
- A reflection test compares Record json tags (including nested user) with the schema properties and required list in both directions.
- A leak-guard test fails when an exported analytics.Event field is neither mapped in FromEvent nor listed in an explicit excludedEventFields list (SecretRef, Evidence and others).
- A negative test proves that a fake secret value, SecretRef, Evidence strings and header names (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key) never appear in emitted bytes.
- Validation uses the reflection checker plus a per-property type check, so go.mod gains no JSON Schema library.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add new docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json.
2. New internal/auditlog/schema_test.go: load ../../docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json, compare properties and required with Record tags, and check each property's JSON type against a fully populated marshaled Record.
3. New internal/auditlog/leak_test.go: TestEventFieldsAccountedFor walks reflect.TypeOf(analytics.Event{}) against the mapped and excluded lists.
4. In leak_test.go add TestNoSecretLeak: build an Event with SecretRef, Evidence, a fake secret in the URL query and JudgeReason, write it through a Sink to a buffer, and scan the bytes.
5. Assert the reason enum in the schema equals proxy.Reasons() from W-P1-JAUD-06.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Adding a field to Record but not the schema, or the reverse, makes `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestDecisionRecordMatchesSchema` fail and name the field.
- [ ] Adding an exported field to analytics.Event without mapping or excluding it makes `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestEventFieldsAccountedFor` fail and name the field.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestNoSecretLeak` passes and finds no secret value, SecretRef, Evidence or header name in the output.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 5/6 · W-P1-JAUD-03

**Write CP admin audit lines as warden.admin.v1 JSON**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#68](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/68)

Let the control plane read the same audit.jsonLog block and pass an auditlog writer to the admin audit middleware from W-P1-AAUD-02, so every CP mutation also produces a warden.admin.v1 line for the SIEM. The line is written only after the admin audit row is stored, and a write failure never fails the admin request. This ticket also owns docs/schemas/warden.admin.v1.json, because the admin record only exists after W-P1-AAUD-02.

**Requirements**

- cmd/proxy/controlplane.go runControlPlane builds the writer when pol.Audit.JSONLog.Enabled and passes it to the middleware through a new controlplane.Config field; cmd stays construction only.
- New closed AdminRecord: schema warden.admin.v1, schema_rev, ts, cp_id, boot_id, seq, actor{sub, email, role}, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, outcome (ok|denied|rejected|error, the W-P1-AAUD-02 set), before_hash, after_hash, request_id, and chain_seq, entry_hash, prev_hash and key_id copied from the stored admin_audit row so the shipped copy anchors the chain. The periodic `admin_audit.checkpoint` lines from W-P1-AAUD-02 are written as warden.admin.v1 records too. Request bodies, tokens and cookies are never fields.
- The line is written after adminaudit.Store.Append succeeds, through an adminaudit.Emitter (the W-P1-AAUD-02 seam), outside the chain mutex. A write error logs a rate-limited WARN (the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1) and does not roll back the stored row or change the response.
- Denied (403) mutations are written with outcome denied.
- The existing admin_audit operational log line stays unchanged whether or not the sink is enabled; with output stdout the CP operational logger moves to stderr.
- Default off: with audit.jsonLog absent or disabled, CP behaviour is unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/auditlog/admin.go: AdminRecord and a WriteAdmin(rec AdminRecord) method on the sink, sharing the queue, caps and metrics from W-P1-JAUD-01.
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: construct the sink with Meta{ProxyID: hostname, ProxyIDSource: hostname}, set the new controlplane.Config.AuditLog field, close it on shutdown, and move the operational logger to stderr for stdout output.
3. internal/controlplane: when the writer is non-nil, register an adminaudit.Emitter (W-P1-AAUD-02 seam) that builds AdminRecord from the stored entry and calls WriteAdmin, chained after the default slog emitter.
4. Add new docs/schemas/warden.admin.v1.json and internal/auditlog/admin_test.go with the same closed-field reflection test as W-P1-JAUD-02.
5. Tests in internal/controlplane: policy save, viewer 403, disabled sink and failing writer cases.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With audit.jsonLog enabled and output file, an admin policy save adds exactly one line with schema warden.admin.v1, outcome ok, actor.sub set and before_hash different from after_hash: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminAuditJSONSink`.
- [ ] A viewer's policy save that returns 403 adds one line with outcome denied, and the policy is unchanged.
- [ ] With the sink disabled, the operational logger still records admin_audit and no audit file is created.
- [ ] With a writer that errors, the policy save still returns 200 and the admin audit chain still verifies.
- [ ] A request body field named token with a value never appears in the emitted line.

### 6/6 · W-P1-JAUD-04

**Document SIEM shipping with Vector and Fluent Bit examples**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#69](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/69)

Write docs/siem.md so operators can turn on the decision and admin streams and ship them to a SIEM. Ship the Vector and Fluent Bit examples as real files, add a compose override that enables the stream on a shared volume, and check the docs against the schemas in the default test gate. Running the shipper binaries is an opt-in integration step.

**Requirements**

- docs/siem.md explains the streams versus operational logs, the audit.jsonLog config, a field table for both schemas checked against docs/schemas, the reason set, the versioning rule, and gap detection with boot_id and seq.
- Rotation and retention guidance: typical bytes per line, how to size maxSizeMB and maxBackups, and that the SQLite store and receipts stay the record of truth.
- Security guidance: default fileMode 0600, using fileMode 0640 with a shared group for a shipper running as another UID, read-only mounts for sidecars, TLS to the SIEM endpoint, the PII note on user.email, and that path segments are not scrubbed.
- Example files docs/siem/vector.yaml (file source, JSON parse, route on schema, http or splunk_hec sink with a console alternative) and docs/siem/fluent-bit.conf (tail input, json parser, rewrite on schema).
- Kubernetes guidance: output stdout with a node-level collector filtering on the schema key, operational logs on stderr.
- New deploy/compose/docker-compose.siem.yml override enables audit.jsonLog output file on a shared volume and runs Vector with a file sink.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write new docs/siem.md and the new docs/siem/vector.yaml and docs/siem/fluent-bit.conf.
2. Add new deploy/compose/docker-compose.siem.yml used with deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml.
3. New internal/auditlog/doc_test.go: TestSIEMDocFieldsMatchSchema parses the field tables in docs/siem.md and compares them with both schema files.
4. scripts/check.sh: under the existing --integration flag, run vector validate and fluent-bit --dry-run when the binaries are present.
5. Add a link to docs/siem.md from docs/architecture.md and the README docs list.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A field documented in docs/siem.md but missing from the schemas, or the reverse, makes `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestSIEMDocFieldsMatchSchema` fail and name the field.
- [ ] `vector validate --no-environment docs/siem/vector.yaml` exits 0 under `scripts/check.sh --integration`.
- [ ] With the compose override up, one allowed and one denied request produce two events in the Vector file sink with schema warden.decision.v1 and decision allow and deny.
- [ ] `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.
